topic: Day 26 uncredited preview: Antimagnetic rotation (AMR) in 110Cd and J^(2)/B(E2) diagnostic ratio

collective_rotation_well_deformed.Delta_I_sequence: Delta I = 2 cascade, strong E2 crossovers
collective_rotation_well_deformed.angular_momentum_generation: Collective rotation of distorted mass distribution

magnetic_rotation_MR.Delta_I_sequence: Delta I = 1 M1 cascade with weak/absent E2 crossovers
magnetic_rotation_MR.angular_momentum_generation: Closing of proton-particle and neutron-hole shears blades

antimagnetic_rotation_AMR.Delta_I_sequence: Pure Delta I = 2 E2 cascade with no M1 transitions
antimagnetic_rotation_AMR.angular_momentum_generation: Simultaneous symmetric closing of two opposing shears

falsification_insights: 110Cd exhibits a nearly constant B(E2) ~ 0.10 e^2b^2 from 12+ to 16+, disproving the simplistic universal hard gate that AMR B(E2) must steeply drop by factors of 3-5
The ratio J^(2)/B(E2) ~ 245 - 329 hbar^2 MeV^-1 (e^2 b^2)^-1 is an order of magnitude higher than collective rotation (~20-40), providing the robust discriminator
Complete absence of M1 transitions is enforced by the double-shears inversion symmetry, cleanly separating AMR from MR and wobbling
